preview.headline: Dave brings leftovers. Murphy needs a proper dinner.
preview.summary: Thanksgiving preview after Green Bay–Los Angeles: Sharpe has 19.52 from two starters and a 5–6 record that keeps annoying the rankings. Murphy is 3–8, favoured again, and running out of weeks in which that means anything.

sections.title: The waiver habit is catching
sections.text: Dave added Mumpfield on Wednesday evening and got 10.90 straight away. Love supplied only 8.62, leaving two slots used for a modest lead. After beating Joe by 0.62, Sharpe remains in the four-team queue at 5–6 despite scoring 203.34 fewer season points than Murphy. The man whose profile used to say he never touched the wire has started shopping. Unfortunately, the quarterback aisle still offers no refunds.

sections.title: Aidan serves the expensive course
sections.text: Prescott and Cook play on Thanksgiving, giving Murphy two early chances to make that lead disappear. London and Judkins provide the weekend muscle. Meyers carries a Questionable tag in the morning Sleeper snapshot; Hutchinson, last week’s $26 purchase, is now on the bench. Aidan lost by 2.90 to Alan and needs wins much more than another argument about how respectable his roster looks.

sections.title: The Thanksgiving call: Aidan Murphy
sections.text: Murphy at 1/3. His available scoring options outweigh Dave’s banked start, with McMillan’s Questionable tag adding a Monday complication for Sharpe. Dave has already made us regret backing Joe. Doing it again would be impressive; Murphy making us regret trusting his team would be rather more familiar.

preview.headline: One seat left. Burns and Joe brought their own chairs.
preview.summary: Thanksgiving preview after Green Bay–Los Angeles: sixth-placed Joe leads Burns by 21.14 season points, with both at 5–6. Kyren has put Burns 16.50–4.90 ahead. The commissioner’s perfect playoff attendance now faces an unusually direct inspection.

sections.title: The last-seat argument
sections.text: Joe’s 0.62 defeat to Dave has invited three other 5–6 teams into the conversation. Burns arrives from 135.10 against Tommy and gets to challenge the man occupying sixth. With three regular-season games left, the winner gains a full win on the loser. Neither can clinch the place here. Ennis has spent years specialising in fourth; he now has someone trying to repossess sixth.

sections.title: The opener favours the host
sections.text: Kyren’s 16.50 beats Golden’s 4.90, while Swift and Kelce give Burns Thanksgiving involvement against Joe’s St. Brown and LaPorta. Purdy missed Wednesday practice with an ankle sprain and could miss Sunday. Joe’s only other rostered quarterback is Hurts on IR. That requires attention before the leftovers, even with Skattebo and Nabers giving the rest of his lineup plenty of promise.

sections.title: The Thanksgiving call: Emmet Burns
sections.text: Burns narrowly, at 10/11 to Joe’s 11/10. Chase and Collins give the commissioner enough to defend the early advantage, with Shough currently selected ahead of Nix. Purdy’s availability could swing this. Six seasons of perfect playoff attendance is a lovely dinner-party fact; losing this one would make Burns considerably less keen to bring it up.

preview.headline: Alan wants the head of the table back.
preview.summary: Thanksgiving preview after Green Bay–Los Angeles: Shane and Alan meet at 8–3, separated by 46.88 season points. Shane has eleven from the Rams defence. Alan has five straight wins and the increasingly inconvenient responsibility of defending an actual title.

sections.title: First place gets personal
sections.text: Shane’s last three scores all exceeded 143; Alan won last week with 98.40. Both approaches count the same in the win column, but Marmion’s recent scoring earns the edge here. The Rams have already supplied eleven, and Smith-Njigba returns from his bye. Shane being this attentive in November is bad news for anyone who had pencilled in his annual disappearance.

sections.title: Horgan brings the main course
sections.text: Gibbs and Burden play in the early Thanksgiving game, with Burrow and Brown still to come Sunday. Bowers and Diggs carry Questionable tags in the morning feed; Alan has Waller and Perine among his alternatives. Shane also needs to follow Smith-Njigba’s Questionable tag. The selected-lineup PPR estimates are only 0.14 apart, before replacing the Rams projection with their recorded return. This should demand more than the champion’s usual proof of purchase.

sections.title: The Thanksgiving call: Shane Marmion
sections.text: Shane at 10/11, narrowly ahead of Alan at 11/10. Recent form and the banked defence points make the case, with Lamb playing tonight and Kittle available Sunday. Karl is also 8–3, so the winner still has company in the bye race. Horgan can explain that in next week’s round-up if he loses.

preview.headline: Keenan eats early. Tommy studies the menu.
preview.summary: Thanksgiving preview after Green Bay–Los Angeles: Keenan has Watson’s 16.50 banked and five more selected players in Thursday’s games. Tommy is 3–8, one win above Hugo, and has bought another quarterback to explain the situation to.

sections.title: Andrew has a busy Thursday
sections.text: Goff, Barkley, Emmett Johnson, DeVonta Smith and Aubrey are all due on Thanksgiving. Jacobs was inactive for the opener and stayed on Keenan’s bench; Christian Watson’s points count despite his subsequent Out tag. Walker’s confirmed absence keeps Johnson central to Andrew’s plans. Two consecutive wins have restored a 7–4 record. The 2021 champion can finally discuss something that happened after the league reached twelve teams.

sections.title: Tommy changes the person holding the clipboard
sections.text: O’Brien paid $5 for Deshaun Watson and dropped Rodgers on Wednesday. Watson is selected; Stafford’s 3.60 remains on the bench. Moore and Loveland give Tommy a Thanksgiving answer, while Irving waits until Monday. Tuten’s Questionable tag needs checking before Sunday. Last week’s 101.08 lost to Burns, and a third Wall of Shame appearance remains a much more pressing subject than another theoretical breakout.

sections.title: The Thanksgiving call: Andrew Keenan
sections.text: Keenan at 8/13. His early points and remaining backfield offer the stronger case, though Flowers is still Questionable in the feed. Tommy at 13/8 has enough through Irving and Stevenson to make this awkward. The football expert needs the score to support the lecture before Hugo starts tuning up underneath him.

preview.headline: Two former forfeits would prefer a quiet holiday.
preview.summary: Thanksgiving preview after Green Bay–Los Angeles: Hugo starts with Kraft’s 3.40 and a 2–9 record. Jack is 7–4 after Shane dismantled last week’s feature. Neither needs reminding what happens when the league gets to choose your extracurricular activities.

sections.title: Hugo needs a result to match the recovery
sections.text: Walsh scored 121.86 against Karl and still lost. His recent improvement has not moved him off the bottom, with Tommy and Murphy one win ahead. Caleb Williams and Javonte Williams give him two Thanksgiving chances to repair Kraft’s modest start; Taylor and Higgins follow Sunday. The $4 Strange pickup stays on the bench. Buying a second tight end is sensible. Getting the first one to score would be more immediately helpful.

sections.title: Jack would like the camera turned off
sections.text: Ringrose followed 172.04 with 102.86, making our decision to back him against Shane look rather generous. Allen and Jameson Williams play Thursday, with McCaffrey and Jefferson anchoring the weekend. Henry and selected tight end Fannin carry Questionable tags; Kincaid, his rostered alternative, is questionable for Thursday night. Jack needs to check that cover before Buffalo kicks off.

sections.title: The Thanksgiving call: Jack Ringrose
sections.text: Jack at 8/11, with Hugo 11/8. Allen, McCaffrey and Jefferson favour a rebound, although Hugo’s improved scoring deserves respect. A Walsh win would tighten the forfeit fight. Ringrose has already contributed a calendar to league culture; helping another manager escape the basement would be a less revealing contribution.

preview.headline: Karl has already gone back for seconds.
preview.summary: Thanksgiving preview after Green Bay–Los Angeles: Corum has delivered 28.50 for Karl before the turkey is served. Niall is 5–6, Walker is out again, and the 8–3 opponent has somehow found another reason to stop complaining about his schedule.

sections.title: Corum starts the feast
sections.text: Moroney selected Corum and has the full 28.50 safely banked. Coleman, last week’s 34.90 hero, plays Friday; Bijan is back from his bye. Add Daniels, Pickens and McBride and the best-lineup price makes Karl the week’s shortest favourite. Any forthcoming complaint about bad luck should be submitted with a copy of Wednesday’s receipt.

sections.title: Niall checks who is actually coming
sections.text: Walker is ruled out with the groin injury and is on Murray’s bench. Dowdle currently joins Hall in the starting backfield. Evans and Likely carry Questionable tags, with Evans absent from Wednesday practice. Niall has Gesicki available at tight end and Douglas among his receiver alternatives. He trails Joe by only 23.26 season points, but last week’s 97.04 showed how quickly the playoff pursuit can stall.

sections.title: The Thanksgiving call: Karl Moroney
sections.text: Karl at 2/7, Niall at 10/3. Lawrence, Olave and Washington give Murray a route back, but chasing Corum with this many availability checks is a difficult assignment. Alan and Shane play each other, making this a useful opportunity in Karl’s bye chase. Niall would happily accept a plain sixth-place finish without the dessert menu.
